hook: Voyager 1 survived a 48‑hour silence 24 billion km from Earth.

sections.voiceover: Voyager 1 survived a 48‑hour silence 24 billion km from Earth.
sections.visual_cue: Voyager 1 image with distance overlay showing 24 billion km.

sections.voiceover: In September 2026, NASA engineers performed a power-saving swap by disabling three devices on Voyager 1. Did the 48-hour communication blackout on October 20, 2026, resolve itself for the Voyager team?
sections.visual_cue: Diagram of power swap showing three devices turned off and three low‑power units activated.

sections.voiceover: Voyager 1 drifted 24 billion kilometers from Earth when the Deep Space Network lost signal.
sections.visual_cue: Graphic of Voyager 1 location 24 billion km from Earth with blackout icon.

sections.voiceover: The Voyager 1 signal returned automatically after 48 hours of silence on October 20, 2026. NASA engineers swapped three devices for lower-power alternatives to keep the 1977 probe active.
sections.visual_cue: Animation of signal returning, data stream to Deep Space Network, and 1977 launch badge.

sections.voiceover: Voyager 1's journey continues, still powered by ingenuity.
sections.visual_cue: Voyager 1 sailing through interstellar space, caption “still powered by ingenuity”.
